item: Goodman's Project Apollo approved after 541 days, with a single public objection
actor: NSW Department of Planning, Housing & Infrastructure
grounds: Process / consultation / transparency; Water use
frame_summary: SSD-74069708 determined on 2 September 2026: 135 MW, ~A$1.365bn, 4-10 Talavera Road Macquarie Park. item: Hazelmere residents & objectors — 1,836 objections to GreenSquareDC data centre
actor: Local residents and objectors (Hazelmere / City of Swan)
grounds: Noise; Environmental or ecological; Water use; Health; Land use / amenity / visual
frame_summary: Public comment on the 120MW Hazelmere proposal drew 1,897 submissions, of which 1,836 were objections. Grounds cited: diesel back-up generator noise, heat output, electromagnetic energy and exhaust emissions, plus proximity (~40m) to the Helena River, a conservation wetland, two Aboriginal heritage sites and the Helena River Steiner School. The campaign preceded GreenSquare's withdrawal on 14 May 2026.

item: [2025-11-27] Victoria announces $5.5M Sustainable Data Centre Action Plan — plan document never publicly released
actor: Department of Jobs, Skills, Industry and Regions (Victorian Government)
grounds: Energy load or grid; Water use; Jobs / investment / economic; Process / consultation / transparency; Climate or emissions
frame_summary: Victorian Government frames the plan as a whole-of-government coordination framework to unlock up to $25 billion in projects and position Victoria as the Asia-Pacific hub for sustainable data centres, addressing energy, water, workforce and governance through coordination and expectations rather than binding regulation. PUBLICATION STATUS (verified 2026-08-17): announced 27 Nov 2025 by the Premier; the DJSIR webpage (~Feb 2026, page updated Aug 2026) is the only public artifact — no plan document has ever been released. In the Legislative Council (4 Mar & 13 May 2026) David Ettershank noted the plan "is referenced repeatedly on the government's website… yet it is not downloadable"; departmental contacts suggested it "has not been produced yet or is for internal government use only". A documents motion passed 13 May 2026 requiring tabling within 30 days; as of late June 2026 Ettershank was still calling for its public release.
representative_quote: 'the Asia-Pacific hub for sustainable data centres'

item: Hume City Council motion — first VIC council to build a data-centre assessment framework
actor: Hume City Council (Cr Naim Kurt — corrected 2026-08-16; agent had misread the name as "Jim Kurt", no such councillor)
grounds: Water use; Energy load or grid; Process / consultation / transparency; Land use / amenity / visual
frame_summary: On 25 Aug 2025 Hume endorsed a motion to draft a framework assessing data-centre applications against sustainable resource use and to call on the Victorian Government to strengthen planning controls — the first Victorian council to act. Concerns: enormous water/energy load, developers bypassing council via ministerial fast-track (some applications surfaced only via FOI), ~7 data centres incoming to Hume plus 20-30 across the west, and Yarra Valley Water fielding 7 cooling-water draw applications (one approved at up to 3.94 million m3/yr).
representative_quote: They are a wicked problem. They're huge in scale, consuming massive amounts of water and electricity whilst offering little back to the community in terms of jobs.
